commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use and disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as this BAA permits.
commitments.scope: All PHI (as defined in the HIPAA Rules, including limited data sets per Section 2.4) that ExampleCo creates, receives, maintains or transmits for Example Health System and its affiliated hospitals and clinics under any Underlying Agreement.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions in the Agreement, DPA and configuration. The BAA instead limits use and disclosure to what is necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, required by law or permitted by the BAA, and covers all PHI rather than only Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may de-identify PHI only under the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the de-identified data only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: PHI de-identified under the safe harbor method. Once de-identified this way, the data is no longer PHI and falls outside the BAA, but its use remains limited to providing and improving the Underlying Agreement services.
commitments.deviation: DPA 8.2 lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services, with no prescribed de-identification method. The BAA requires the HIPAA safe harbor method and limits use to providing and improving the services under the Underlying Agreements. It does not address AI model training (DPA 8.1) or model provider retention (DPA 8.3).

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule for ePHI.
commitments.scope: Electronic PHI that ExampleCo handles for Covered Entity.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to the Annex 2 Security Measures and lets ExampleCo update them if overall security is not materially reduced. The BAA instead requires full compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule's administrative, physical and technical safeguards, which ExampleCo cannot unilaterally update.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not store or process PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, in any form.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data at rest in the hosting region Customer selects. The BAA imposes a fixed United States-only requirement covering both storage and processing.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not access PHI from outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including access by ExampleCo personnel and, through the Section 5.1 flow-down, by Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: DPA 6.2 permits access from outside the hosting region for support, maintenance and security, including from the Manila, Philippines support center, under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism. The BAA prohibits all access to PHI from outside the United States, which rules out the Manila support model for PHI.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001, or substantially equivalent successor standards. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 certification specifically, which is not part of the DPA commitment.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach under 45 C.F.R. § 164.410(a)(2). This is the first day the Breach is known to ExampleCo or, by exercising reasonable diligence, would have been known to any workforce member or agent of ExampleCo other than the person who committed it.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example, in writing (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI as defined in the HIPAA Rules, in any form. An impermissible use or disclosure is presumed to be a Breach unless a low probability of compromise is shown. Confirmation by ExampleCo is not required.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. The BAA gives a longer 10 calendar days, but the clock starts at Discovery, which includes constructive knowledge of any workforce member or agent, rather than at confirmation. Breach also covers all Unsecured PHI under the HIPAA presumption, not only confirmed security breaches. Where the Breach involves ePHI, the 5-business-day Security Incident report in Section 4.2 may fall due first.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the Security Incident (ExampleCo's actual awareness).

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example, in writing (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Security Incidents under 45 C.F.R. § 164.304: attempted or successful unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification or destruction of information, or interference with system operations. This is limited to ePHI that ExampleCo or its Subcontractors handle for Covered Entity. Unsuccessful attempts are addressed by the standing notice in the rest of Section 4.2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice only of confirmed Personal Data Breaches and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The BAA requires a report of every Security Incident, including attempted incidents and incidents not confirmed as breaches. The deadline is 5 business days from awareness rather than 72 hours from confirmation.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: Section 4.2 itself serves as standing notice of unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI, so no separate report is needed for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from the Personal Data Breach definition, which also lists denial-of-service attacks. The BAA treats such attempts as Security Incidents but deems them reported by this standing notice. Its examples do not include denial-of-service attacks, which may interfere with system operations and so may need a report.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must report any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo becoming aware of the impermissible use or disclosure.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example, in writing (Section 4.4).
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI, in any form, not permitted by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach or a security event.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no duty to report non-security impermissible uses or disclosures. It notifies only confirmed security breaches within 72 hours of confirmation. The BAA adds this separate 10-calendar-day reporting duty, which runs from awareness.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must send all Section 4 reports in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example.
commitments.scope: All reports under Section 4: Breaches, Security Incidents and impermissible uses or disclosures.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the administration console, or else to the account owner. The BAA fixes two contractual email addresses and requires written reports to both.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, each affected individual's identity, the PHI involved, the dates of the Breach and its Discovery, and the mitigation steps taken.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ehs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ehs.example.
commitments.scope: Reports of Breaches of Unsecured PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA notice covers the nature of the breach, the categories of data and the measures taken, and promises further information as it becomes available. The BAA requires individual-level identification of affected persons, the specific PHI involved, and the Breach and Discovery dates. It has no express duty to provide updates.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors.
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI caused by ExampleCo or its Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must ensure each Subcontractor handling PHI agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to ExampleCo under the BAA.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors under 45 C.F.R. § 160.103 that create, receive, maintain or transmit PHI on ExampleCo's behalf.
commitments.deviation: The DPA keeps ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessor performance and provides 30-day notice, objection and urgent-replacement mechanics (5.1–5.4). The BAA instead requires a written flow-down of all BAA terms, including US-only storage and access and HITRUST obligations. It has no subcontractor notice or objection mechanism.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days after its request so Covered Entity can meet individual access obligations.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request.

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary for HIPAA compliance determinations.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats the SOC 2 and penetration test reports as satisfying audit rights. It allows a further on-site audit only when a supervisory authority requires one, once per 12 months, with 60 days' notice, at Customer's expense. The BAA grants the HHS Secretary access to records with none of those limits.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, ExampleCo must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days.

deadline.anchor: Termination of the Underlying Agreements.

commitments.scope: All PHI in any form, including copies held by Subcontractors through the Section 5.1 flow-down.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes data within 90 days after termination, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days, and provides a deletion certificate on request. The BAA requires return or destruction of all PHI within 30 days and makes no separate allowance for backups.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If returning or destroying PHI is not feasible, ExampleCo must keep applying the BAA's protections to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.scope: PHI whose return or destruction is not feasible, which may include backup copies.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility exception and no continuing-protection obligation. It relies on backups being overwritten within 35 days.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier. Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides any conflicting Supplier document, including Supplier's DPA, and terms on Supplier's trust or security site do not bind Bank.
commitments.scope: All Supplier documents, including the ExampleCo DPA and Trust Center terms; this most affects incident notice, subprocessor, audit and deletion terms.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says it controls over the Agreement as to processing. Here the Bank Addendum controls over the DPA itself, and Trust Center-incorporated terms have no effect.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a written security program consistent with the NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA refers to Annex 2 measures that ExampleCo may update unilaterally. Here the program is tied to the named NIST and FFIEC frameworks, with no right to update unilaterally.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data with AES-256 or stronger at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including metadata, logs, configuration data and derived, aggregated or de-identified data.
commitments.deviation: Same encryption standard, but it is a fixed contractual obligation covering the broader Bank Data definition, rather than only Customer Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require MFA for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
commitments.scope: All systems of Supplier that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for production systems. Here MFA covers all remote access to any system handling Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must complete criminal background checks on all Supplier and Subcontractor personnel before they access Bank Data, where lawful.

deadline.anchor: granting the person access to Bank Data

commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, meaning employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires only written confidentiality obligations for personnel. It has no background check requirement.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services for the full term.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, or substantially equivalent successor standards. Here a current SOC 2 Type II is required with no substitution allowed, and ISO 27001 is not required.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Supplier must store and process Bank Data only in the United States.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including derived and de-identified data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only storage at rest in the customer-selected region. Here both storage and processing are restricted to the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No Supplier or Subcontractor personnel outside the US may access Bank Data, even for support, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel, including Subcontractor personnel.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region, including from the Manila support center, under the SCCs. Here offshore access is prohibited without Bank's prior written approval.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 may access Bank Data, and each only within its stated scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors, including Supplier Affiliates and any third party with access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA grants general authorization using the Trust Center list. Here there is a closed list with per-subcontractor scope limits.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give at least 90 days' prior written notice to Bank TPRM before adding or replacing a Subcontractor or expanding a Subcontractor's scope.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, tprm-notices@enb.example, with a copy to Example National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001
commitments.scope: New or replacement Subcontractors and scope expansions.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 30 days' notice through a Trust Center update and email to subscribers, and DPA 5.4 allows urgent replacement without prior notice. Here 90 days' direct written notice is required, it also covers scope expansions, and there is no urgent-replacement exception.

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days for any reason; if it does, Supplier may not use the Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services with a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the Subcontractor notice

commitments.deviation: The DPA allows objection within 15 days only on reasonable data protection grounds, with termination as the sole remedy after 30 days. Here Bank has 30 days, needs no stated grounds, and Supplier must not engage the Subcontractor; Bank may alternatively terminate without penalty and get a refund.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations at least as protective as the Addendum to every Subcontractor.
commitments.scope: All Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within 6 hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Subcontractor's Discovery (when the Subcontractor knew, or with reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident)

commitments.scope: Security Incidents, including suspected incidents and unauthorized access to Subcontractor systems.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable for its Subcontractors' acts and omissions.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes ExampleCo responsible only for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. Here Supplier is fully liable for all their acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and no later than 12 hours after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery, meaning the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or with reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@enb.example
commitments.scope: Security Incidents: actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to or use, disclosure, alteration or destruction of Bank Data, or unauthorized access to any Supplier or Subcontractor system handling Bank Data, even if data access is unconfirmed.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach. Here the limit is 12 hours from actual or constructive knowledge by Supplier or any Subcontractor, and it covers suspected incidents and system intrusions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center; notice only to the relationship manager or via a status page or trust site does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center, telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147 and email cfc-thirdparty@enb.example (not the relationship manager Dana Okafor)
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact in the admin console, or to the account owner. Here notice must be by phone and email to a fixed Bank address, and status pages and trust sites are excluded.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include all known information, including the Discovery time, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the affected data categories.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, the data categories and the measures taken, to the extent known. Here the notice must also include all known information, the Discovery date and time, and the systems and Subcontractors involved.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

deadline.anchor: initial Security Incident notice, until containment

commitments.recipient: Bank (Exhibit C lists the Cyber Fusion Center for incident notices: +1 (212) 555-0147, cfc-thirdparty@enb.example)
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires further information only as it becomes available. Here written updates are required at least every 24 hours.

commitments.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: The DPA has no root-cause report requirement.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not notify Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media of an incident without Bank's written consent, unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Supplier must tell Bank before giving any legally required third-party notice, where legally permitted.

deadline.anchor: giving a legally required notice to a third party

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep all forensic evidence of a Security Incident for at least one year after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request
commitments.summary: Supplier must give Bank and its forensic investigator access to preserved evidence on request.
commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: Supplier must reimburse Bank's reasonable investigation and response costs for incidents caused by Supplier or Subcontractors, including notification costs and 24 months of credit monitoring.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. DPA 7.4 says notification is not an acknowledgment of fault, and the DPA has no cost reimbursement.

commitments.quote: Supplier's obligations to ENB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds obligations owed to ENB Securities LLC.
commitments.scope: ENB Securities LLC customer information.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: Where more than one notice period applies to the same notice, the shortest controls, so the 12-hour period in 6.1 governs over the 72-hour periods in Exhibit D and the DPA.
commitments.scope: All notice periods in the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules and applicable law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any AI model except one used solely for Bank's Services.
commitments.scope: Bank Data, including metadata, logs, model outputs, embeddings and aggregated or de-identified derived data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models offered to other customers, and DPA 8.2 lets ExampleCo use aggregated Usage Data to improve the Services. Here any model use (including evaluation and improvement) is barred except Bank-only models, and aggregated or de-identified data counts as Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: No one may review, label or annotate Bank Data for model development unless Schedule 2 expressly permits it.
commitments.scope: The only permitted case is Labelforge annotating de-identified feedback samples submitted by Bank, for improving Bank's own agents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall identify in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data
commitments.summary: Every third-party model provider receiving Bank Data must be listed in Schedule 2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lists model providers on the Trust Center. Here they must appear in the contractual Schedule 2.

commitments.quote: shall ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response
commitments.summary: Supplier must ensure no model provider keeps Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.scope: All third-party model providers.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows retention for abuse monitoring and only requires ExampleCo to impose the requirement on providers. Here zero retention must be ensured, with no abuse-monitoring exception.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least once every twelve (12) months, and shall deliver an executive summary of the results to Bank within thirty (30) days after Bank's request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must have an independent penetration test every 12 months and deliver the executive summary within 30 days of Bank's request.

deadline.anchor: previous penetration test

secondary_deadline.anchor: Bank's request for the executive summary

commitments.deviation: The DPA makes the summary available through the Trust Center. Here it must be delivered directly to Bank within 30 days of request.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Supplier must fix Critical vulnerabilities within 15 days and High vulnerabilities within 30 days of identification.

deadline.anchor: identification of a Critical vulnerability

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall deliver its SOC 2 Type II report to Bank within thirty (30) days after the report is issued, and a bridge letter on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver each SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of issuance, and a bridge letter on request.

deadline.anchor: issuance of the SOC 2 Type II report

commitments.deviation: The DPA makes the report available on the Trust Center subject to NDA terms. Here it must be delivered proactively within 30 days, plus bridge letters, and Trust Center terms do not bind Bank.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Bank, its auditors and regulators may audit once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on 5 business days' notice.

deadline.anchor: the routine annual audit

secondary_deadline.anchor: an audit following a Security Incident

commitments.deviation: The DPA treats reports as satisfying audit rights and allows an on-site audit only when a supervisory authority requires it, with 60 days' notice, at Customer's expense. Here audits are allowed annually on 30 days' notice and after incidents on 5 business days' notice, with no cost-shifting.

commitments.quote: Nothing in this Addendum limits the access of any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.summary: Regulators with authority over Bank keep unrestricted access.
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits audits to one per year. Here regulator access is unlimited.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a recovery time objective of no more than four (4) hours and a recovery point objective of no more than one (1) hour.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a BC/DR plan with an RTO of 4 hours or less and an RPO of 1 hour or less.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a BC/DR plan with no RTO or RPO targets.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall test the plan at least annually, provide Bank a summary of the results
commitments.summary: Supplier must test the BC/DR plan at least annually and give Bank a summary of the results.

deadline.anchor: previous BC/DR plan test

commitments.deviation: The DPA requires annual testing but no results summary for the customer.

commitments.quote: participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on sixty (60) days' written notice
commitments.summary: Supplier must take part in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on 60 days' notice.

deadline.anchor: Bank's operational resilience exercise (Bank's notice period)

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of no less than twenty-five million dollars ($25,000,000) per claim throughout the term of the Agreement and for two (2) years after.
commitments.summary: Supplier must carry cyber liability insurance of at least $25M per claim during the term and for two years after.

deadline.anchor: end of the term of the Agreement

commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request, Supplier shall return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests and then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Within 30 days after termination or Bank's request, Supplier must return Bank Data and then destroy all copies, including backups and copies held by Subcontractors.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request

commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including backups and Subcontractor copies.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows 90 days for deletion plus 35 more days for backups, with no return and no deletion on request. Here return and full destruction, including backups, are due within 30 days and can be triggered on request.

commitments.quote: Within ten (10) business days after destruction, Supplier shall deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer of Supplier.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver an officer-signed certificate of destruction within 10 business days after destruction.

deadline.anchor: destruction of Bank Data

commitments.deviation: The DPA provides certification only on written request, with no deadline. Here an officer-signed certificate is automatic within 10 business days.

commitments.quote: Sections 6, 10 and 11 survive termination of the Agreement for as long as Supplier or any Subcontractor holds Bank Data.
commitments.summary: The incident, insurance and return/destruction sections survive termination while any Bank Data is held.
commitments.scope: Sections 6, 10 and 11.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Infrastructure hosting | All Bank Data, US regions only | United States
commitments.summary: AWS may host all Bank Data, but only in US regions.
commitments.scope: Infrastructure hosting; US regions only.
commitments.deviation: The DPA uses the Trust Center list with no per-subprocessor scope limits. Here AWS is limited to US regions.

commitments.quote: Model Provider A, Inc. | Large-model inference for AI agent features | Prompts and outputs only; zero retention | United States
commitments.summary: Model Provider A may receive only prompts and outputs, with zero retention, in the US.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs only; zero retention; United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits abuse-monitoring retention by model providers. Here zero retention is required and processing is limited to the US.

commitments.quote: Labelforge, Inc. | Human annotation of feedback samples | Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents. Bank Data in identifiable form is not permitted. | United States; US-based annotators only
commitments.summary: Labelforge may annotate only de-identified feedback samples Bank submits, only to improve Bank's own agents, using US-based annotators only.
commitments.scope: De-identified Bank-submitted feedback samples only; no identifiable Bank Data; US-based annotators only.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no scope limits on subprocessors. Here human annotation is confined to Bank-submitted, de-identified samples for Bank's own benefit.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | Contact details of Bank users only | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform may process only Bank users' contact details, in the US.
commitments.scope: Contact details of Bank users only; United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no scope limits on subprocessors. Here the support tool is limited to contact details and to the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify ENB Securities LLC as soon as possible, but no later than seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system maintained by Supplier.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify ENB Securities LLC within 72 hours of becoming aware of a security breach giving unauthorized access to a customer information system, but Section 6.8 makes the 12-hour period in Section 6.1 control.

deadline.anchor: Supplier becoming aware of a breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system maintained by Supplier

commitments.recipient: ENB Securities LLC (no separate contact is given; Exhibit C directs Security Incident notices under Section 6.1 to the Bank Cyber Fusion Center, +1 (212) 555-0147, cfc-thirdparty@enb.example)
commitments.scope: Customer information of ENB Securities LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer.
commitments.deviation: The DPA uses 72 hours after confirmation. This term uses 72 hours after awareness, but Section 6.8 displaces it in favor of the 12-hour period in Section 6.1.

commitments.quote: This Exhibit supplements, and does not replace, Section 6 of the Addendum.
commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds to Section 6 and does not replace it, so the Section 6 incident duties still apply to ENB Securities data.
commitments.scope: ENB Securities LLC customer information.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA overrides the Subscription Agreement and any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates, including ExampleCo's standard DPA.
commitments.scope: Applies against all Vendor and Vendor Affiliate terms. ExampleCo, Inc. is a Vendor Affiliate (Appendix B Amendment No. 1), so ExampleCo's DPA (72-hour notice after confirmation, Trust Center notices, Manila access, 90-day deletion) cannot displace the VDPA for Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline makes the ExampleCo DPA control over the Agreement for personal data processing. Here the customer's VDPA prevails over all vendor and affiliate terms, so the DPA's breach timeline, subprocessor and deletion terms yield to the VDPA.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, meaning all data provided by Retailer, its employees or customers or collected from Retailer systems (including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics) and all derived data, not only personal data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline covers only Customer Personal Data and treats configuration of the Services as an instruction. The VDPA covers all Retailer Data, including derived data and telemetry, and requires written instructions.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any ML model other than models used solely to serve Retailer.
commitments.scope: Any machine learning model and all Retailer Data, including telemetry, logs, metrics and derived data. It reaches ExampleCo, which is approved for AI features.
commitments.deviation: The baseline bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models offered to other customers, and 8.2 permits use of Usage Data to improve the Services. The VDPA bars any training or improvement of any model except Retailer-only models, and because derived data is Retailer Data, the Usage Data carve-out is effectively unavailable.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Vendor must store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Storage of all Retailer Data, including by Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: The baseline stores data in the customer-selected region and 6.2 allows access from outside that region, including from Manila. The VDPA fixes storage to the US or Canada. It does not expressly restrict remote access, but Appendix B approves ExampleCo only with a United States location, and the VDPA prevails over DPA 6.2.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards that meet or exceed CIS Critical Security Controls IG2.
commitments.deviation: The baseline points to vendor-defined Annex 2 measures that the vendor may update unilaterally. The VDPA sets an external benchmark (CIS Controls IG2) with no unilateral change right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: The baseline specifies AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 or higher in transit. The VDPA uses a general industry-standard requirement but applies it to all Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain an annual SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.

deadline.anchor: each year

commitments.scope: The Services provided to Retailer.
commitments.deviation: The baseline requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, or substantially equivalent successor standards. The VDPA requires an annual SOC 2 Type II only, with no successor-standard substitution.

commitments.quote: provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must deliver the SOC 2 Type II report to Retailer within 15 days after Retailer requests it.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request for the SOC 2 report

commitments.deviation: The baseline makes the report available via the Trust Center subject to Trust Center NDA terms. The VDPA requires direct delivery within 15 days, with no NDA condition, and does not treat reports as satisfying audit rights (contrast DPA 9.3).

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Only Appendix B Subprocessors may process Retailer Data unless Retailer gives prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Any third party, including Vendor Affiliates such as ExampleCo, that processes Retailer Data. ExampleCo's own subprocessors (e.g., AI model providers, Manila support) are not listed and would need consent.
commitments.deviation: The baseline grants general authorization with a list on the Trust Center. The VDPA uses a closed list and requires prior written consent for anything else.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request written consent at least 30 days before a new Subprocessor starts processing, and silence is not consent.

deadline.anchor: new Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.scope: Any new Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives 30 days' notice by Trust Center update and email to subscribers. The customer may object within 15 days (5.3), with termination as the sole remedy, and urgent replacement without prior notice is allowed (5.4). The VDPA requires an affirmative written consent request, treats silence as no consent, and has no urgent-replacement exception.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA
commitments.summary: Vendor must contractually flow down obligations at least as protective as the VDPA to each Subprocessor.
commitments.scope: Every Subprocessor, including ExampleCo. This requires flow-down of the 24-hour Data Incident notice, US/Canada storage and the AI training restrictions.
commitments.deviation: The baseline has no express written flow-down requirement. The VDPA requires written terms at least as protective as the VDPA, so ExampleCo's standard 72-hour, confirmation-based terms would not suffice.

commitments.quote: remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor remains liable for all acts and omissions of its Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: The baseline makes the vendor responsible only for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations. The VDPA imposes liability for all Subprocessor acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of any Data Incident without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor (XYZwire) becomes aware of an actual or reasonably suspected Data Incident; no confirmation required

commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations: email secops@erg.example and telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, any Retailer Data (not only personal data), including while held by a Subprocessor such as ExampleCo.
commitments.deviation: The baseline gives 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach and excludes unconfirmed or unsuccessful events. The VDPA gives 24 hours from awareness, covers suspected incidents, all Retailer Data and Subprocessor-held data, and prevails over ExampleCo's terms under Section 1.1.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@erg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Data Incident notice must go by email and telephone to Retailer Security Operations, and notice to account or procurement contacts does not count.
commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations: email secops@erg.example and telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.deviation: The baseline sends notice to the security contact designated in the admin console, or else the account owner. The VDPA fixes dual-channel delivery (email and phone) to SecOps and expressly excludes account or procurement contacts.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.summary: The notice must describe the incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved and the steps Vendor has taken.
commitments.deviation: The baseline requires content only to the extent then known and does not require identification of Subprocessors. The VDPA adds Subprocessor identification and has no 'to the extent known' qualifier.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Vendor must supplement its Data Incident notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.deviation: This is substantially similar to the baseline's commitment to provide further information as it becomes available.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not tell Retailer's customers or third parties about a Data Incident without Retailer's prior written approval, unless the law requires it.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation of a Data Incident.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.summary: Vendor must bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent Vendor or its Subprocessors caused it.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents caused by Vendor or any Subprocessor, including ExampleCo.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The baseline 7.4 instead states that breach notification is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends.

deadline.anchor: end of the Subscription Agreement

commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data and, with no backup carve-out, backups and Subprocessor copies.
commitments.deviation: The baseline allows 90 days for deletion plus a further 35 days for backups to be overwritten, and covers only personal data. The VDPA requires deletion of all Retailer Data within 30 days, with no backup extension.

commitments.quote: confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing
commitments.summary: Vendor must confirm deletion to Retailer in writing.

deadline.anchor: end of the Subscription Agreement

commitments.deviation: The baseline provides certification only on the customer's written request. The VDPA requires written confirmation automatically.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's VDPA compliance once each calendar year on 30 days' notice.

deadline.anchor: start of the audit (Retailer's notice)

secondary_deadline.anchor: calendar year (one routine audit per year)

commitments.scope: Compliance with the whole VDPA.
commitments.deviation: The baseline treats SOC 2 and pen-test reports as satisfying audit rights and allows an on-site audit only where a supervisory authority requires one, on 60 days' notice, during business hours, at customer expense. The VDPA gives a direct annual audit right on 30 days' notice with no regulator trigger or cost allocation to Retailer.

commitments.quote: within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident
commitments.summary: After a Data Incident, Retailer may audit Vendor within 10 days after giving notice, outside the annual limit.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's audit notice following a Data Incident

commitments.scope: Audits following any Data Incident, including suspected incidents.
commitments.deviation: The baseline has no incident-triggered audit right. The VDPA allows an expedited audit on 10 days' notice after a Data Incident.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.scope: All VDPA obligations, including the 24-hour incident notice.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not terminate or change the VDPA.
commitments.scope: Any merger or acquisition of Vendor, including by ExampleCo, which is now a Vendor Affiliate.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: An acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data without Retailer's written agreement.
commitments.scope: Retailer Data. ExampleCo's standard DPA (72-hour, confirmation-based notice and other terms) does not apply unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.deviation: Under the baseline, the ExampleCo DPA governs by acceptance. Here ExampleCo's standard terms are excluded for Retailer Data absent Retailer's written agreement, so the VDPA's 24-hour notice and other terms govern.

commitments.quote: Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Hosting | United States
commitments.summary: Amazon Web Services is an approved Subprocessor for hosting in the United States.
commitments.scope: Hosting only, United States location.
commitments.deviation: The baseline uses a vendor-maintained Trust Center list. The VDPA fixes approved Subprocessors in a contractual appendix with a stated purpose and location.

commitments.quote: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | United States
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. is an approved Subprocessor for support ticketing in the United States.
commitments.scope: Support ticketing only, United States location.
commitments.deviation: The baseline uses a vendor-maintained Trust Center list. The VDPA uses a fixed contractual list with a stated purpose and location.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions, which are set out in the Agreement, this DPA, and Customer's configuration of the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions as set out in the Agreement, the DPA and Customer's configuration.
commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data, meaning Personal Data in Customer Data that ExampleCo processes on Customer's behalf.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will ensure that personnel authorized to process Customer Personal Data are bound by written obligations of confidentiality.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must bind personnel who process Customer Personal Data to written confidentiality obligations.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will implement and maintain the technical and organizational measures described in Annex 2 ("Security Measures").
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must implement and maintain the Security Measures described in Annex 2.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may update the Security Measures from time to time, provided that updates do not materially reduce the overall security of the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may update the Security Measures, provided the updates do not materially reduce overall security of the Services.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services, or successor standards that are substantially equivalent.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification, or substantially equivalent successor standards, for the Services.

commitments.quote: Customer grants ExampleCo general authorization to engage Subprocessors. The current list of Subprocessors is published on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Customer gives ExampleCo general authorization to engage Subprocessors, and ExampleCo publishes the current list on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Any third party engaged by ExampleCo that processes Customer Personal Data; list published at trust.exampleco.example.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will give notice of any new Subprocessor at least thirty (30) days before the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data, by updating the Trust Center list and emailing Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must give at least 30 days' notice of a new Subprocessor by updating the Trust Center list and emailing subscribed Customers.

commitments.scope: Any new third party engaged by ExampleCo that processes Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor on reasonable data protection grounds by written notice within fifteen (15) days after ExampleCo's notice. commitments.summary: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor within 15 days of notice on reasonable data protection grounds, and if the objection is unresolved within 30 days may terminate the affected Services as its sole remedy.

commitments.summary: ExampleCo may replace a Subprocessor urgently without prior notice for security or continuity reasons but must notify Customer promptly afterward.
commitments.scope: Urgent replacements needed to protect security or continuity of the Services.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo remains responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of the obligations in this DPA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo remains responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations.

commitments.quote: Customer Personal Data will be stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects for its Services.
commitments.summary: Customer Personal Data must be stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects.
commitments.scope: Storage at rest only; does not restrict remote access.

commitments.summary: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from outside the hosting region, including Manila, for support, maintenance and security operations.

commitments.quote: Any transfer is made under the transfer mechanism in Annex 3.
commitments.summary: Any transfer of Customer Personal Data is made under the Annex 3 transfer mechanism.

commitments.recipient: Security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console, or, if none is designated, Customer's account owner

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will send notice to the security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console. If no security contact is designated, ExampleCo will send notice to Customer's account owner.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.

commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
